instruction.text: You’ve just learnt about the obligations of a local authority. There’s still one important obligation left. Put the name of the last obligation together.

atoms.a: What must every local authority organise to choose their representatives?

atoms.b: When an election is held, the ((++citizens mayors)) vote for someone to represent them.
Local elections choose the councillors that work in local authorities. General elections choose someone to represent the ((++local_area house)) in the UK government.
((++All No)) British citizens are allowed to vote if they are at least ((++18 8)) years old.

feedback.end: In Scotland and Wales, you can vote in a local election from the age of 16 - but you still need to be 18 for a general election!

atoms.b: UK elections use a ((open ++secret)) vote, where no one knows who you have voted for. This is usually done by marking the candidate you are voting for on a ((++ballot_paper ballot_stone)).

instruction.text: Decide if the statement is true or false.

atoms.a: In local elections in Scotland and Wales, citizens who are at least 14 can vote.

instruction.text: Decide if the statement is true or false.

atoms.a: In a secret vote, everyone knows who you have voted for.
In a secret vote, no one is allowed to see who you have voted for. Votes are made with ballot papers.

instruction.text: Imagine that you are allowed to go and vote. Put the steps of doing a secret vote in the correct order.

finish.text: After the election, all the votes will be counted, and the winner will be revealed.

atoms.text: Inform yourself about the candidates before the election.
On the election day, go to the polling station at the correct time.
At the polling station, vote by marking a cross on the ballot paper.
After you have made your vote, put your ballot paper in the box.
